description: The tool is published on npm as feature-ledger. You install it once with `npm install -g feature-ledger` and run `ledger` in any project, add it to a JavaScript project with `npm install --save-dev feature-ledger`, or run any command through `npx feature-ledger` without installing anything. Using it no longer means keeping a checkout of the tool itself.

While a first edition is in progress, including the first edition after a redraft, the Markdown docs tag no entry as New. With nothing earlier to compare with, every entry would carry the tag, and the PDF already prints those editions without flags.

Every command that prints a prompt for a coding agent (ledger bootstrap, ledger style rewrite, ledger audit, ledger review and ledger redraft check) takes --print, which prints the prompt alone. You can pipe it straight to the clipboard, for example with ledger review --print | pbcopy. Warnings print on your screen rather than into the pipe. See “Handing a task to a coding agent” for the other ways to deliver a prompt.
Adding --help or -h to any command prints that command's part of the help and runs nothing. For example, ledger cut --help never cuts a release.

Every command refuses an option it does not take, and runs nothing. The error names the option, suggests the one you probably meant, and lists the options that the command takes. For example, ledger cut --dryrun stops with "did you mean --dry-run?" instead of cutting the release.

The commands read as words you can guess: ledger cut, ledger releases and ledger subcategories replace ledger release cut, ledger release list and ledger subcategory. The old names still work and say what they are called now. A mistyped command is answered with the closest one, the exit code tells a mistake (2) from a check that said no (3), and ledger completion adds tab completion to zsh, bash and fish.
